About the opportunity

We are looking for an AFC Senior Associate / SAR Delegate to join our French MLRO Team. In this pivotal role, you will serve as a primary point of contact and decision-maker for Anti-Financial Crime (AFC) Operations - driving quality and consistency across SAR submissions, ongoing due diligence, Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), and complex investigations.

Joining a diverse, highly motivated team in a fast-paced, tech-driven environment, you will act as a vital bridge between our local branch Compliance/AFC function, AFC Operations, and Global teams. Beyond internal leadership, you will also represent the business in direct communications with the FIU and other requesting authorities.

In this role, you will:

• Oversee complex case investigations, sanctions reviews, and other AFC related processes

• Review and submit SARs, ensuring quality according to Tracfin and ACPR expectations

• Review complex Authority Requests

• Assist AFC Operations on their investigations

• Provide guidelines individually and collectively. Prepare and deliver formal training to AFC Operations

• Prepare necessary templates for AFC Ops communication with customers

• Implement and improve local procedures based on the local regulatory challenges and the group’s standard

• Coordination with other operational functions working on the French market

What you need to be successful:

Background:

•
Graduated in law (Ecole de droit/Master II) or from a Grande Ecole - or alike.

•
At least 5 years of professional experience gained in anti-financial crime.

•
Proven experience in operational functions, including investigation, and SAR drafting but also transaction monitoring, sanctions and adverse media screening.

Skills:

•
In-depth knowledge of European and French regulations on Financial Crime (KYC, AML, terrorism financing, fraud, tax evasion, sanctions…).

•
Deep investigation expertise.

•
French as mother tongue, fluency in French and English spoken and written.

•
Excellent written skills in French.

•
Excellent communication skills and ability to work with a wide variety of stakeholders.

•
Proven ability to liaise with the French Authorities.

•
Hardworking, strong team player, benevolent and resilient.

•
Diligent and reliable, solution driven and committed, ability to work under pressure.

•
Strong analytical, advisory skills, high quality standards and attention to detail.

•
You have a hands-on mentality and take ownership.

•
You should enjoy a fast-paced working environment, show high willingness to learn and work autonomously to grasp new topics.

Traits:

•
Actively help yourself (and others) to be successful.

•
Continuously learn and challenge the status quo.

•
Think globally, act locally.

•
Benevolent and demanding.

What’s in it for you:

• Accelerate your career growth by joining one of Europe’s most talked about disruptors 🚀.

• Employee benefits that range from a competitive personal development budget, work from home budget, discounts to fitness & wellness memberships, language apps and public transportation.

• As an N26 employee you will have access to a Premium subscription on your personal N26 bank account. As well as subscriptions for friends and family members.

• Additional day of annual leave for each year of service.

• A high degree of autonomy and access to cutting edge technologies - all while working with a friendly team of peers of diverse nationalities, experiences, and backgrounds.

• A relocation package with visa support for those who need it.

Who we are

N26 has reimagined banking for today’s digital world. Technology and design empower everything we do and it’s how we are building the global banking platform the world loves to use.

We've eliminated physical branches, paperwork, and hidden fees for an elegant digital experience and supreme savings. Giving people the power to live and bank their way is what gets us out of bed in the morning and inspires the work that we do.

We are headquartered in Berlin with offices in multiple cities across Europe, including Madrid and Barcelona, and a 1,700-strong team of more than 80 nationalities.

Do you see yourself thriving in this role? We’d love to see your application even if you don’t meet 100% of the criteria. You may just be the right fit for this or other roles!

Equal opportunities for all

At N26, we believe our strength lies in our people and the varied perspectives they bring. We strive to build diverse teams that drive innovation and business success. We actively seek talent from all backgrounds and welcome applications from all genders, cultures, sexual orientations, abilities, neurodiversities, and ages.

We are committed to providing an excellent and accessible candidate experience. If you require any accommodations to make this process work for you, please let us know. We’re here to support you!

🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.

📍London / UK Remote | 💰 Staff Backend Engineer (L60) £130,000 - £170,000 + Equity + Benefits | Technology - Engineering

About our Engineering Teams:

We have around 650 engineers out of roughly 5,500 people in total - and we have big ambitions. There are many interesting challenges ahead, and we're happy for people to move between teams or to specialise, whatever you prefer. As an engineer here you'd be able to work directly with anyone across the company, and we run regular knowledge-sharing sessions so you’ll learn heaps about everything from how banks work to effective communication.

We contribute to open source software as much as possible. Our blog is a good place to learn even more about what we do!

What you’ll be working on:

We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies:

• Go to write our application code (there’s an excellent interactive Go tutorial here )

• Cassandra for most persistent data storage

• Kafka for our asynchronous message queue

• Envoy Proxy for RPC

• Kubernetes and Docker to schedule and run our services

• AWS for most of our infrastructure

• React for internal web dashboards

• We also have two physical datacenter sites with actual cables to connect to various third parties

Your day-to-day

This role is all about collaborating across disciplines to test hypotheses and make a difference to customers. As a product backend engineer you’ll work in a squad alongside product managers, marketers, user researchers, designers, mobile engineers, web engineers, data analysts, business analysts, writers and more!

Together you'll build and support a particular part of Monzo. Our squads belong to our wider collectives (a word we use to describe self-governing business units of ~100 people). Our collectives are doing innovative work, many of which have machine learning and AI at the forefront - from fighting financial crime to building smarter financial tools - and you may have the opportunity to join a collective that gives you direct exposure to this exciting space.

Our backend engineers have a variety of different backgrounds. As long as you enjoy learning new things, we’d love to talk to you. We do not ask for formal qualifications or degree requirements for any of our engineering roles.

How we work 💻

Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles.

We value meeting in person but we don't have a mandated requirement on office attendance, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨

Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.

Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life:

At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance.

You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨

If you prefer to work part-time, we'll make this happen whenever we can - whether this is to help you meet other commitments or strike a great work-life balance.

Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼

You should apply if:

• you have strong experience working on the backend of a technology product

• you want to be involved in building a product that you (and the people you know) use every day

• you have a product mindset: you care about customer outcomes and you want to make data-informed decisions

• you’re comfortable working in a team that deals with ambiguity

• you’re interested in distributed systems and writing resilient software

• you have some experience with strongly-typed languages (Go, Java, C, Scala etc.).

• you think you’d enjoy the kind of work we’re doing

We're on the look out for L60 Engineers at the moment, you can read more in our Engineering Progression Framework we are also hiring on L40 & L50, our interview process will determine your levelling.

The Interview Process:

Our interview process involves three main stages:

• Initial Call

• Take home task or pair coding exercise

• Final interview including a system design and a behavioural interview

Our average process takes around 2-3 weeks but we will always work around your availability.

One of our engineers has written a detailed blog on their experience through this process, for extra details, hints and tips please see here .

What’s in it for you:

💰 £130,000 - £170,000 + Equity

✈️We can help you relocate to the UK

✅ We can sponsor visas.

📍This role can be based in our London office or remotely across the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).

⏰We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.

📚 Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences

➕And much more, see our full list of benefits here

We're usually always hiring for Backend Engineers, so there's no closing date for this job.

#LI-Remote

#LI-HJ1

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog , 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

body:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Safeguards Analyst focusing on Targeting, Tracking & Surveillance, you will be responsible for building and executing enforcement workflows for our products and services, with a focus on detecting and mitigating attempts to misuse Anthropic's AI systems to track, target, or surveil individuals and groups covertly, without their informed consent, or with malicious intent.

Your work will span an interconnected set of harm areas: the use of AI systems to facilitate stalking, the covert monitoring of people's locations, devices, and online activity, the profiling and identification of individuals or groups, and surveillance at scale.

Important context for this role: In this position you may be exposed to and engage with explicit content spanning a range of topics, including those of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature. This role may require responding to escalations during weekends and holidays.

Key responsibilities

•
Design and architect automated enforcement systems and review workflows that scale effectively while maintaining high accuracy

•
Partner with Engineering and Data Science teams to optimize detection models for policy violations and automated enforcement systems

•
Review flagged content to drive enforcement and policy improvements

•
Enforce usage policies with a focus on detecting and mitigating AI-enabled targeting, tracking, and surveillance of individuals and groups, and on distinguishing that activity from legitimate research and journalism

•
Support the Safeguards policy design team by providing detailed feedback on policy gaps based on real enforcement scenarios

•
Collaborate with Policy Managers and Threat Intelligence Investigators to identify emerging trends and flag content for classifier refinement

•
Keep up to date with emerging AI policy enforcement best practices, evolving threat actor tactics, and the regulatory landscape around privacy and surveillance, using these to inform our decision-making and workflows

Minimum qualifications

•
Experience in trust & safety, policy enforcement, threat intelligence, or a closely related field with a focus on privacy and surveillance harms, such as targeting, tracking, stalking, or profiling

•
Experience standing up and scaling policy enforcement or content review workflows

•
Proficiency in SQL and/or other data analysis tools to draw insights from large datasets

•
Experience identifying emerging risks and threat actors, and communicating findings to a diverse set of stakeholders, such as Product, Policy, Engineering, and Legal teams

•
Experience working with generative AI products, including writing effective prompts for content review and enforcement

•
Understanding of the challenges involved in implementing product policies at scale, including in the content moderation space

Preferred qualifications

•
Experience conducting cross-platform investigations into targeting, tracking, or surveillance activity and the threat actors behind it

•
Familiarity with open-source intelligence (OSINT) techniques and tools used for threat actor tracking and network analysis

•
Working knowledge of privacy law, surveillance technology, or data broker ecosystems as they relate to targeting and tracking harms

•
Experience with large language models and an understanding of how AI technology could be misused to locate, identify, profile, or monitor people at scale

•
Experience navigating evolving regulatory landscapes relevant to this space (e.g., DSA, EU AI Act, GDPR)

•
Experience working with civil society organizations or government agencies on privacy or surveillance-related issues

•
Proficiency in Python for data analysis and automation

•
Experience with dark web monitoring or tracking threat actors across surface, deep, and dark web environments

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$245,000 — $285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Building the supermarket on wheels

Started in 2015 in the Netherlands, Picnic now delivers groceries to millions across three countries, growing fast. The idea? We’re bringing back the milkman. Imagine personal service and fresh products but in a modern, sustainable way. We’re looking for bright minds to shape the future of grocery shopping with us. Ready to join the revolution?

Tech at Picnic

At Picnic we merge advanced technology with a customer-centric approach. We aim to create a simple, affordable, and enjoyable grocery shopping experience. Work on various aspects like our mobile app, store backend, internal development platforms, delivery routing, warehouse logistics, and ML models – all built in-house. We’re looking for problem-solvers who thrive in a collaborative environment. We are open to junior and experienced software, data and ML engineers. Our diverse team welcomes innovative and bold ideas.

1. With a diverse team of over 80 nationalities, you’re sure to find your people

“At Picnic, we build the technology that powers the transition towards a sustainable food

waste. The team behind this innovation loves to crack hard problems, uses data to

explore unbeaten paths, and strives to stay ahead of the curve in this fast-paced

industry.”

– Daniel Gebler, CTO

Our Java teams in the Warehouse Systems domain are the reason why our warehouses can process the volume of groceries they do! From dealing with inbound items, to sending totes across the warehouse on conveyor belts, to sending the groceries off to our delivery drivers - our software developers build tools and automations to power the entire warehouse platform. About the opportunity

Wealth is where customers grow their money with N26. It spans the full journey: saving day to day, putting idle cash to work in flexible cash funds, investing in stocks, ETFs and crypto, and understanding how it all adds up. That means the experience around savings, flexible cash funds, asset discovery, orders, and portfolio, and the connections between them. Customers increasingly move between these spaces, and our job is to make that feel like one clear, trustworthy experience. Assets under custody have more than doubled in the last year, and the number of products and initiatives in Wealth keeps growing.

You'll work across the domain rather than on a single product area. Depending on what the team needs, that could mean designing how customers discover and understand flexible cash funds, refining the order flow and order history, helping customers read and act on their portfolio, bringing clarity to asset discovery and asset detail pages, or designing the interaction patterns and data visualisations (like performance charts) that make complex financial information easy to grasp. You'll work on self-contained initiatives of low to mid complexity, with guidance from your paired designer, and your scope will grow as you do.

You'll be designing for a regulated financial product used by millions, where trust, clarity, and detail matter. The bar is high, and the work matters.

In your next challenge, you will:

• Design well-scoped features and improvements across Wealth, from understanding the problem through exploration to shipped work.

• Design intuitive interactions and polished interfaces, with careful attention to edge cases and error states.

• Help customers understand products like flexible cash funds, where clear explanation and the right moment to surface them make the difference.

• Use and contribute to our design system, Pulse, keeping your work consistent with the patterns the team relies on.

• Plan and run simple usability tests and interviews, and turn what you learn into clear, actionable insights.

• Use data to understand how customers behave and to check whether your work is making a difference.

• Partner closely with product, engineering, research, and data to ship work that lands, and learn from it once it's live.

• Explain the "why" behind your decisions to your team, and seek feedback early and often.

• Use AI tools as part of your design practice, for exploration, prototyping, and synthesis.

• Share what you learn with your peers and suggest improvements to how the team works.

What you’ll need to be successful

• You're fluent in Figma, and you keep getting better at it. You build with Auto Layout by default, so designs behave properly across screen sizes, languages and dynamic content. You work with components, variants and variables, and you move quickly with commands and shortcuts instead of reaching for the mouse. A tidy, well-named file is part of your craft. You're not satisfied with "good enough" in the tool and enjoy learning new features and techniques, then sharing them with the team.

• You're curious about the problem before the solution. You ask who the user is, what they need, and what constraints you're working within.

• You like to ship. You prototype to learn, share work early, and prefer real feedback over polishing in isolation.

• You're curious about money, saving and investing, or willing to become so. You don't need to be an expert, but you want to make complex financial topics easy for everyone to understand.

• You use AI to work better, not to skip the thinking. You're curious about how AI is changing design and product, and you use it to explore options, prototype and synthesise research faster. You also know it doesn't replace good craft or judgement. You can tell when an output is generic, inaccurate or wrong for a regulated financial product, and you take responsibility for the final result.

• You think beyond the single screen. You see how savings, funds, orders, and portfolio connect, and you design with the wider journey in mind.

• You're a generous collaborator. You give and receive feedback well, and you want to make the work better, not just your part of it.

We are headquartered in Berlin with offices in multiple cities across Europe, including Madrid and Barcelona, and a 1,500-strong team of more than 80 nationalities.

📍London or UK Remote | 💰 Senior Engineer (L50) £105,000 - £135,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits | Technology - Engineering

About our Engineering Teams:

We have around 650 engineers across Monzo who design and build our in-house banking platform. We have big ambitions for the future, and technology plays a big role in creating a bank our customers want, so engineers at Monzo collaborate across disciplines to solve interesting challenges throughout the company.

These range from the products our customers use everyday to underlying infrastructure, security, payments and finance, customer operations, financial crime, and data, to name just a few areas. As a bank, there is scope for impact across a huge number of opportunities.

We contribute to open source software as much as possible. Our blog is a good place to learn even more about what we do!

Your day-to-day

This role is all about collaborating with your team to make a difference to your customers. As a backend engineer you’ll work in a squad alongside other disciplines like product managers, marketers, user researchers, designers, mobile engineers, web engineers, data analysts, business analysts, writers and more!

Together you'll build and support a particular part of Monzo. Our squads belong to our wider collectives (a word we use to describe self-governing business units of ~100 people). They are: Core Banking, Business Banking, Wealth, Borrowing, Growth, Payments, Platform, Fincrime, Security & Expansion. All of our collectives are doing innovative work, many of which have machine learning and AI at the forefront- from fighting financial crime to building smarter financial tools - and you may have the opportunity to join a collective that gives you direct exposure to this exciting space.

They’re all looking for additional Backend Engineers right now, we do a standard interview process across all our collectives and at the end we will find the best match for you based on your skills, experience, preferences and aligning with the business need!

Our backend engineers have a variety of different backgrounds. As long as you enjoy learning new things, we’d love to talk to you. We do not ask for formal qualifications or degree requirements for any of our engineering roles.

How we work 💻

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. We value meeting in person but we don't have a mandated requirement on office attendance, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs ✨

Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️

Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼

• you want to be involved in building a product that you (and the people you know) use every day

• you have a product mindset: you care about customer outcomes and you want to make data-informed decisions

• you’re comfortable working in a team that deals with ambiguity

• you’re interested in distributed systems and writing resilient software

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Integrity & Compliance team helps the company meet its legal and regulatory obligations as our products, customers, and global footprint grow. We're looking for a Manager, Compliance & Regulatory Operations to lead the team that handles regulatory requests and complaints, copyright notices, and sanctions screening and operations.

We're looking for an excellent operations manager. You'll manage a team and own how the work gets done: the queues, the systems, the operating model, and the outsourced partners who extend the team. The work is both high volume and high consequence. Some of these processes are established and need to scale. Others are still being built. Volumes are growing quickly across all of them, so you'll be running today's queues while designing the systems that will carry the next stage of growth. Claude is central to that plan, and you'll decide where it can take on the work and where people need to stay involved.

You'll work closely with our Regulatory Programs team as well as other I&C teams, who own the design and management of our regulatory and compliance programs. Your team runs the operations that put those programs into practice, working to the policy and standards those teams set. You'll also partner with Legal, Safeguards, Threat Intelligence, Engineering, and Support.

This is an operations leadership role, not a legal one. You need to understand how regulatory and compliance processes work, why these processes matter, and when a decision belongs to someone else.

Key responsibilities

• Lead, coach, and develop a team across regulatory, copyright, and sanctions operations, and build cross-coverage so that no queue depends on a single person

• Design and own the function's operating model, including how work comes in, who handles it, when it escalates, and what stays in-house or goes to outsourced partners

• Manage queues across the team day to day, meeting SLAs and matching staffing to volume and priority

• Own intake, case management, service levels, and escalation paths across the team, and lead decisions on our case management system

• Lead the team's use of Claude, working with Engineering to automate triage and routine work, deciding which steps need human judgment, and checking the quality of what is automated

• Manage outsourced providers day to day, including performance, service levels, procedures, and commercial terms

• Set up a clear way to evaluate and accept new requests and projects, and make tradeoffs visible to stakeholders

• Plan for sudden increases in volume, including surge coverage for complaint spikes and new product launches

• Lead operational readiness for new products, business initiatives, and workflows, partnering with program owners, Legal, and Product so that requirements, controls, and capacity are in place before launch

• Define and report the operational metrics that show leadership and auditors how the team is performing, such as volume, handling time, SLA adherence, quality, and backlog

• Oversee operational support for recurring regulatory reporting and ad hoc data requests, ensuring program owners and Legal receive accurate, well-documented data on time

• Run quality assurance on operational decisions against defined criteria, and turn the findings into training and process changes

• Own and maintain operational procedures for each program, working to the standards program owners set and securing their approval of changes

• Oversee regulatory operations, including triaging new requests, seeing them through to completion, and responding to complaints and inquiries across jurisdictions

• Oversee copyright operations from intake through resolution, including takedown notices, opt-out requests, appeals, and repeat infringement tracking

• Oversee sanctions screening operations, including referrals from partner teams, so that work meets SLAs and is escalated appropriately

Minimum qualifications

• Significant people management experience in an operations environment, including setting priorities, coaching, and managing performance

• Hands-on ownership of a high-volume compliance, regulatory, or similarly high-consequence operation with service levels, escalation paths, and quality checks

• Track record of designing or significantly changing an operating model, including roles, handoffs, capacity, and what is kept in-house or outsourced

• Experience managing outsourced vendors or managed service providers against performance and quality standards

• Working knowledge of case management or workflow systems, including how to shape them around a team's process

• Hands-on automation of operational work, including deciding what can be automated and checking the results

• Procedure writing and recordkeeping that have held up to audit or regulatory review

• Ability to analyze queue and case data and turn it into staffing and process decisions

• Track record of taking a manual or inconsistent process and turning it into a repeatable, scalable, well-documented one

• Strong cross-functional skills, including working with Legal, Compliance, and technical teams, influencing without direct authority

• Sound judgment about which decisions you can make and which belong to Legal, policy owners, or leadership

• Interest in AI and a commitment to Anthropic's mission of building safe, beneficial AI systems

Preferred qualifications

• Sanctions operations experience, including restricted-party screening, alert disposition, and screening tools, ideally at a technology, payments, fintech, or financial services company

• Familiarity with DMCA and other copyright notice processes

• Exposure to online content or AI regulation, such as the EU Digital Services Act or EU AI Act

• Background in privacy operations, such as data subject requests and user escalations

• Experience handling regulator inquiries or consumer complaints across multiple jurisdictions

• Experience supporting audits or regulatory reviews

• Prior work selecting, implementing, or migrating a case management system

• A track record of using Claude or other AI tools to automate triage or routine decisions, with quality checks that hold up to review

• Comfort managing a team across time zones

• Success stepping into an operations team during a reorganization or period of rapid growth

Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect staff to be able to work from our Washington, DC, San Francisco, or New York City office at least 3 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period.
The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$270,000 — $345,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Priorities change quickly in research, so we value strong fundamentals over narrow specialisation. When it makes sense, we publish papers and release models and code.

Train and post-train LLMs and multimodal models on multi-node GPU clusters using SFT, preference optimisation, RL (e.g. GRPO), and on-policy and offline distillation.

Design compression techniques (quantization, pruning, quantization-aware training, quantum-inspired tensor-network methods) and healing recipes that recover the quality of compressed models.

•
Build RL environments, reward functions and verifiers for reasoning, coding and agentic tasks, and extend RL methods to world models and Physical AI.

•
Research and prototype post-transformer and hybrid architectures (state-space models, linear attention, MoE), from small-scale ablations to scaling recipes.

•
Build data pipelines for curation, filtering, deduplication and large-scale synthetic data generation.

•
Design rigorous ablations and evaluations on current benchmark suites (reasoning, coding, long-context, instruction following, agentic) as well as internal evals.

•
Port and optimise models for inference on various accelerators and edge chips, profiling latency, memory and throughput.

•
Write up experiments and results as internal reports and, where relevant, papers and open-source releases.

•
Review code, mentor teammates, and follow and bring in the latest research.

Your qualification

•
Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, AI, Mathematics, Physics or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.

•
Senior: 4+ years of hands-on experience training or post-training transformer models.

•
Strong PyTorch. You are comfortable working below library level: model code, custom losses, parallelism configuration.

•
Experience with distributed training (FSDP, DeepSpeed or Megatron-LM; data, tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism) on multi-node clusters with Slurm/K8s.

•
Hands-on post-training experience: SFT, DPO, and at least one RL method (PPO, GRPO or similar).

•
Solid mathematical foundations in linear algebra, optimisation and probability, and an understanding of training dynamics.

•
Good understanding of GPU fundamentals: memory hierarchy, mixed precision, profiling, throughput.

•
Rigorous experimental practice: ablation design, reproducibility, experiment tracking, noise-aware evaluation.

•
Strong debugging and communication skills. Fluent English.

Will be a plus

We don’t expect anyone to have all of these. Our research covers many areas and nobody on the team is an expert in all of them. If you have deep experience in some and none in others, we still want to hear from you.

Experience with the NVIDIA stack (Megatron-LM, Megatron Bridge, NeMo RL, NeMo Gym, NeMo Curator) or similar frameworks (verl, TRL, OpenRLHF).

Multimodal model training (vision-language, audio).

Large-scale data processing and synthetic data generation.

Evaluation tooling (lm-evaluation-harness, lighteval, NeMo Evaluator) and familiarity with Artificial Analysis.

Publications at top venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, etc.), notable open-source contributions, or models released on Hugging Face.

Spanish.

Both startup and enterprise-scale company experience

Working closely with research to translate capability into shipped product

Ecosystem partnerships and MCP, CI/CD, or source-control integrations

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$1 — $2 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems

Comfortable with python

Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities

A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to convey complicated topics in easily understandable terms to a diverse set of external and internal stakeholders. You enjoy engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

We're looking for engineers to join Model-to-Product Behavior Engineering, the team responsible for getting Claude's behavior right across Anthropic's products. You'll work with product, research, and safeguards teams to make sure Claude behaves in ways that are consistent, safe, and genuinely helpful, whether in a new feature, a new model, or a launch.

Evals are one of the sharpest tools we have for getting Claude's behavior right, but not the only one. You'll build evals to see clearly where Claude shines and where it slips, use what you learn to inform how to close the gap, and build the harness improvements that get us there. That takes your own intuition and judgment about model behavior, both to decide what is worth building and to know what to do with what you find. Your work will shape launch decisions and give research and product teams a signal they can trust.

You'll also build the infrastructure behind our evals, along with tooling that makes it easy to test and ship prompt fixes. And you'll create self-serve tools that let other teams build their own evals and improve Claude's behavior in their products, so that getting model behavior right scales well beyond any one team.

You'll work across many projects and product surfaces at once, holding a high bar for the details while adapting as model capabilities change.

Key responsibilities

•
Build evals that measure Claude's quality, behavior, and capabilities across Anthropic's products and model releases, with sound methodology: deciding what to measure, validating datasets and graders, and interpreting noisy results with statistical rigor

•
Apply judgment to model outputs to separate real regressions and capability gaps from noise, and turn findings into clear recommendations

•
Support model launches by catching regressions before they reach users and giving decision-makers a clear read on model readiness

•
Act on what the evals show: build and ship improvements to the product harnesses Claude runs in so that the behavior is right in the product

•
Design, build, and operate the infrastructure our evals run on, and the tooling to test and ship prompt fixes

•
Build self-serve tools and frameworks that let other teams develop and run their own evals and improve model behavior with confidence, and help product engineers build their first evals

•
Set technical direction for our eval and harness systems, and lead projects that span product and research teams

•
Partner with product, research, and safeguards teams to ensure new features and models meet quality and safety standards

Minimum qualifications

•
Strong software engineering skills in Python or a similar language, including version control, testing, and CI/CD

•
Experience owning production systems end to end, from design and architecture through launch and ongoing operation

•
Hands-on experience designing and building evaluations for LLMs, such as datasets, graders, metrics, or eval harnesses

•
Understanding of evaluation methodology for AI systems, including how to validate an eval, the limitations of LLM-based grading, and how to reason about statistical significance

•
Experience building infrastructure, platforms, or developer tools that other engineers or researchers rely on

•
Good judgment about model behavior: you can read model outputs and form a well-calibrated view of what is a real problem and what can be improved

•
Clear communication, in writing and in discussion, including explaining complex model behavior to diverse stakeholders

•
Ability to lead ambiguous, cross-team projects from defining the problem through delivery, and to prioritize across several at once

Preferred qualifications

•
5+ years of software engineering experience

•
Experience using eval results to find and fix problems in an AI product, such as changing a harness and showing the fix worked

•
Background in machine learning, NLP, or a related field

•
Experience with Claude or other frontier AI models in production settings

•
Experience with A/B testing and experimentation frameworks

•
Working knowledge of prompting and context engineering

•
Familiarity with AI safety and alignment considerations

•
Curiosity about how language models behave, and comfort defining success metrics for novel AI capabilities where no standard exists

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$320,000 — $485,000 USD

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. • Drive system card production end to end — own the timeline, the contributor list, the open-threads tracker, and the definition of done for each launch

• Coordinate dozens of contributors across Alignment, Safeguards, Frontier Red Team, Interpretability, and capabilities research; chase drafts, resolve differences of perspective, seek ground truth, and run final formatting and polish

• Edit, and sometimes write, content; work directly with researchers to turn their results, notes, and plots into clear, scientific, non-marketing prose and maintain Anthropic's voice across sections drafted by many different people

• Guard accuracy and consistency; catch terminology drift, claims that subtly contradict each other, and discrepancies between internal communications and system card drafts

• Keep the system card aligned with related artifacts; track what's being said in risk reports, RSP disclosures, and other safety documentation so the system card stays consistent with them, and flag conflicts early

• Improve the process between launches; build and maintain templates, style guidance, contributor guides, checklists, and reusable section scaffolds so each cycle starts from a stronger baseline

• Pick up other research-adjacent operations and writing, such as internal research summaries, release notes, and documentation that helps research leadership communicate clearly

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
